correctness.rationale: Exact residue-threshold proof: write each representation as n=au+2t, where t=y+3z or 2y+3z. For each residue t0 mod a, construct a value <= M with two distinct coefficient vectors, and find one last value M-a having only one. For first family M=a(2k+4)+2(a-1), extremal residue t0=a-1; for second M=a(2k+7)+14, extremal residue t0=7. All remaining j>=1 offsets are explicitly excluded at the last exceptional value by monotone growth of minimal feasible u. The monotonicity r(n+a)>=r(n) closes the entire infinite tail. Exact denumerant dynamic programming corroborates for 66 indices per family, including full tested tails and k=0 exceptions.

value.rationale: The 2021 foundational paper explicitly proposes p-Frobenius numbers for prime k-tuplets as further work. The first positive p case is a nonclassical invariant of exactly its two distinguished prime-triplet-shaped families. Uniform sharp quadratic formulas for every k>=1 reveal two different extremal residues and go beyond known semigroup membership, Apéry and p=0 invariants; the construction is mathematically natural, not an isolated numeric sample.
